questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All cars are vehicles.

All vehicles are trucks.

**Conclusions:**

I) All cars are trucks.

II) All trucks are vehicles

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follows.
Both Conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
**Given:**

**Statements:**

All cars are vehicles.

All vehicles are trucks.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d5f3c72b54aa54f4852e5140c9dc6b3b5c6892cfeea2af53070849f8e11c0f3c.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I) All cars are trucks. → **True** (As it is given that all cars are vehicles and all vehicles are trucks, so it can be said that all cars are trucks).

II) All trucks are vehicles → **False **(It is given that all vehicles are trucks, but it cannot be said that all trucks are vehicles).

So, Only **Conclusion I** follows.

Hence, the correct answer is ***'Option 2'.***
